expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test output and the failing test body before editing source; asks about intended behavior where the spec is ambiguous.
expectations_used.approach: States a hypothesis about the MECHANISM of the failure (what the code does wrong, not merely which file) before changing code.
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates the investigation: what the failure says, what is suspected, what each change is meant to prove.
expectations_used.implement: Makes targeted changes that test the stated hypothesis; instruments (prints/reads state) rather than guessing when stuck.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite after the fix and confirms the previously-failing test passes and nothing else broke.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains the root cause and why the fix addresses it.

summary: The candidate ran the suite, got the failing test, and spent most of the three-minute session reading the assertion diff and browsing shipments.ts and types.ts without ever opening holdStore.ts, where the actual bug lives. No hypothesis about a mechanism was stated, no code was changed, and the session ended before any implementation or verification occurred.

dimensions.analysis: When prompted to explain the failure before diving in, the candidate only offered a generic observation about a deep-equal mismatch without naming which fields, holds, or SKUs were involved, and never opened or quoted the actual failing test body to pin down the scenario (multiple abandoned checkouts). They moved to browsing source files without resolving what specifically was wrong.

No mechanism or even a located hypothesis was verbalized before opening files; they jumped to shipments.ts and then types.ts with no stated reasoning connecting these choices to the deep-equal failure they'd just described, and holdStore.ts — the file with the actual defect — was never opened.

The bulk of the session's speech after the initial exchange is marked as transcription-unavailable, so there is no reliable record of what reasoning, if any, accompanied the file-opening actions. Per the reliability rule, this silence in the transcript cannot be read as absence of narration.
No code edits appear anywhere in the timeline — only file opens (package.json, shipments.ts, types.ts) and the initial test run. The session ended at 180s without any implementation step to assess.
Tests were run once at the very start to observe the failure but never re-run after any change, since no change was made. There is nothing to verify.
The session ended with the candidate clicking End Session with no resolution reached and no discussion of root cause; there was no point where reflection could occur.
